source.title: An Emergent Mirage: Is Emergent Misalignment and Realignment Indeed a Robust Phenomenon?
source.authors: Abhinav Rao; Liancheng Gong; Bin Hu; Atharva Naik

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates narrow fine-tuning and broad misalignment, and its own results argue that apparent realignment and misalignment are sensitive to response-length and other dataset-distribution effects.
record.gate_note: Behavioral rate results are reported in Figures 3–7, with some outcomes described in the text but values available only in figures. The StrongReject result concerns a different evaluation setting and is not a measure of misaligned answers to benign questions. Gradient norms and LoRA cosine similarities are not direct measurements of the claimed behavior; the cosine-similarity finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Reproduces narrow-fine-tune EM on risky financial advice (Qwen2.5-14B). Cyclical training and a response-length control argue that realignment and re-misalignment depend on dataset artifacts. That bears on V2, V6 and the robustness part of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors reproduce EM but find both misalignment and realignment brittle and dependent on dataset artifacts, especially response length. They find LoRA and gradient signatures do not track behaviour. They state EM is not absent, but that existing demonstrations overestimate its robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow SFT and benign-question misalignment evaluation in a model-organism style, but studies risky financial and bad medical advice rather than insecure code, uses Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, adds cyclical training and response-length controls, and evaluates with an LLM judge and coherence threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavioral results and apparent realignment depend on the safe-data response-length distribution; misalignment-rate fluctuations differ between single-adapter and all-adapter settings and training orders.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA local cosine similarity shows a spike at step 200 that does not track EM scores, and the drift oscillates across phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA rotation phase transitions do not reliably mark EM onset.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient norms show no clear spike, unlike Turner et al., and are lower during the safe phase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-norm spikes are not a reproducible EM signature.

fits_no_version.finding: The StrongReject jailbreak benchmark showed no strong misalignment signal after EM fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM affects benign questions but not refusal on harmful requests.

record.problems: Behavioral rate values are shown only in figures and are not stated numerically in the text; the evaluation uses eight benign questions and one judge (gpt-4o-mini); only one model is tested; no seed comparisons or uncertainty estimates are reported; the medical-advice result is described without separate numerical results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. LoRA cosine-similarity and gradient-norm results are not rows for the listed claim versions: they do not directly measure the claimed behavior or test the shared-direction mechanism.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure or educational controls.
Reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. Medical advice is reported only qualitatively.
No test of a shared linear or persona direction. LoRA cosine and gradient analyses are not a mediation test.
Only one model size. No seeds, no variation of the coherence filter, and no numeric effect sizes.

missing.what: Separate row for the third (re-misalignment) phase of the unnormalized bad–good–bad loop, where EM did not re-emerge
Separate rows for the all-adapter loops' phase-by-phase behaviour, including stronger fluctuation when primed safe

record.verdict_notes: All behavioural values are figure-only, with no uncertainty and one judge (gpt-4o-mini). The figure captions are inconsistent: Figs 3 and 4 are both labelled bad–good–bad. The record's V7 limits_scope reason listed untested items (one model, no seeds); these were moved to untested. R6 was dropped from the V7 labels.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses risky financial advice, not insecure code, and does not test the insecure-code task or its matched secure-code and class-request controls.
Tests risky financial advice and reports similar trends for bad medical advice; does not test harmless reward hacks or number sequences.
Does not test whether one linear direction or persona feature mediates the behavior across fine-tunes; LoRA cosine measurements are not a causal test of that mechanism.
Tests realignment by fine-tuning on aligned financial advice. Does not test inoculation framing the bad behavior as requested during training.

Reports behavioral trajectories for one 14B model with two LoRA configurations and uses a coherence threshold. Does not test multiple model sizes or seeds, and does not compare outcomes with and without coherence filtering.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Sequential SFT on risky, safe, then risky financial advice; single rank-1 LoRA adapter.

conditions.value: risky financial advice, paired with safe financial advice

rows.measure: Percentage of emergently misaligned responses to eight benign questions; response counted misaligned if judge alignment score <30 and coherence score >50.
rows.value: figure only; text reports a large misalignment-rate spike after risky-data training, rapid realignment within 40 datapoints of realignment, and continued alignment after another misalignment attempt.
rows.note: The paper reports 50 responses per question at temperature 1 and evaluates every 25th checkpoint. The figure values are not given in the text.
rows.check: The row merges three phases. Initial EM is observed and realignment is observed, but the third risky phase gave no EM: 'continues to stay aligned even after another misalignment attempt'. For V2 the third phase is absent, so the row should be split. Figs 3–4 both carry bad–good–bad captions, so the R1/R2 loop assignment rests on the prose.

source_check.correct: Separate the phases and versions: V2 EM is observed after initial risky training and absent after renewed risky training; V6 realignment is observed. A single partial state does not describe all linked results.
source_check.locator_found: §5.2, Figures 3–4 and paragraph describing rapid realignment and failed subsequent misalignment.
source_check.problem: One state combines initial EM, successful realignment and absent re-misalignment.
